_about: Canonical invariant library — the high-signal backbone the skill instantiates FIRST in Stage 2 (before free-associating from procedures 1-11). Each template is a battle-tested property a skilled auditor writes; the skill binds the schematic symbols (asset/protocol/vault/...) to the target's real identifiers, drops the reference `property` into Properties.sol, and adds the `ghosts` to BeforeAfter.sol. `binds` names what must be mapped; an unbindable template is skipped with a one-line reason, never forced. Prefer FEWER, SIMPLE, grounded invariants over many complex ones. Read with guidance/09-invariant-library.md.

templates.title: Custodied balance covers all obligations
templates.statement: asset.balanceOf(protocol) >= Σ user obligations
templates.tolerance: >= not == : direct donations push the real balance above internal accounting
templates.harm: insolvency — the last users to withdraw cannot be paid (direct loss of funds)

templates.title: Value in equals value out plus value held (no stranded/minted value)
templates.statement: ghostIn == ghostOut + held   (every wei that entered is either still held or left)
templates.tolerance: exact for internal accounting; use approxEqAbs(±1 wei/op) if rounding is expected
templates.harm: value is stranded (locked forever) or created from nothing (dilution / theft)

templates.title: totalSupply equals the sum of balances
templates.statement: token.totalSupply() == Σ balanceOf(actor) over all holders
templates.harm: phantom or destroyed shares — accounting no longer maps to real ownership

templates.title: Paired accounting totals never cross (no underflow)
binds: totalWithdrawn <= totalDeposited, totalRefunded <= totalAllocated, ... (each in<=out pair)
templates.statement: for each paired total: consumed <= provided (validation math never underflows)
templates.harm: an underflow reverts legitimate ops (DoS) or wraps to a huge value (theft)

templates.title: View getters never revert in any reachable state
binds: the protocol's public view getters that other contracts/integrations rely on
templates.statement: core getters return without reverting from any reachable state
templates.harm: a reverting getter bricks integrators / front-ends that depend on it (liveness DoS)

templates.title: A non-privileged actor cannot invoke a privileged action
binds: each privileged setter/mover (setFee, pause, withdrawLiquidity, mint, ...)
templates.statement: a call to a privileged function by a non-authorized actor MUST revert
templates.harm: an attacker seizes an admin power — drain, brick, or re-parameterize the protocol

templates.title: One user's actions never reduce an untouched user's entitlement
binds: victim (an actor not acting this sequence)
templates.statement: a victim who took no action this sequence never sees their entitlement decrease
templates.tolerance: >= (entitlement may grow via yield, never shrink from another's action)
templates.harm: a griefer/attacker steals or destroys a bystander's funds

templates.title: An inverse-operation round trip never profits the user
templates.statement: out(in(a)) <= a  (rounding always favors the protocol)
templates.tolerance: <= a (never > a); a small under-return is fine
templates.harm: a repeatable round-trip gain drains the protocol wei-by-wei (rounding exploit)

templates.title: Share price is not inflatable by a direct donation (first-depositor)
templates.statement: a direct asset transfer to the vault does not let a later depositor be minted 0 shares for a non-trivial deposit, nor let the donor extract more than donated
templates.tolerance: n/a — a non-trivial deposit must mint > 0 shares
templates.harm: classic first-depositor inflation: victim deposits, gets 0 shares, attacker steals it

templates.title: Total owed rewards never exceed the reward pool
templates.statement: rewardToken.balanceOf(protocol) >= _totalOwedRewards()
templates.harm: reward insolvency — later claimers are underpaid or claims revert (DoS/loss)
templates.derived_via: library (proc 3 conservation on the reward path)

templates.title: Accrued rewards equal claimed plus still-claimable (no stranded rewards)
templates.statement: ghostAccrued == ghostClaimed + _totalClaimable()
templates.harm: rewards accrued but permanently unclaimable (stranded value) — or double-counted

templates.title: The constant-product invariant never decreases net of fees
templates.statement: after any swap, reserve0*reserve1 (k) >= k before the swap
ghosts: uint256 k  // set k = reserve0 * reserve1 in __snapshot
templates.tolerance: >= (fees make k grow; it must never shrink)
templates.harm: a swap that lowers k lets an attacker extract reserves (drain the pool)

templates.title: Recorded reserves never exceed real token balances
templates.statement: reserveX <= tokenX.balanceOf(pool) for each reserve
templates.harm: recorded reserves above real balance means the pool cannot honor withdrawals (insolvency)

templates.title: An account stays healthy after any of its own operations
templates.statement: after a borrow/withdraw, the acting account is not left below the liquidation threshold
templates.harm: self-inflicted undercollateralization creates instant bad debt the protocol eats

templates.title: Total debt is backed by total collateral value
templates.statement: Σ debt <= Σ collateral-backing (accounting for the liquidation buffer)
templates.tolerance: <= (a documented dust of bad debt may be tolerated)
templates.harm: unbacked debt means depositors cannot all be repaid (protocol insolvency)

templates.title: Interest / debt index only increases
templates.statement: the accrual index never decreases across any call
templates.harm: a decreasing index silently erases owed interest or corrupts debt accounting

templates.title: Long PnL + short PnL + fees nets to zero
templates.statement: totalLongPnl + totalShortPnl + fees == 0 (a closed system)
templates.harm: non-zero-sum PnL means the protocol prints or destroys value (insurance-fund drain)

templates.title: The insurance fund never goes negative
templates.statement: insuranceFund balance >= 0 at all times
templates.harm: a negative insurance fund is unbacked socialized loss (protocol insolvency)

templates.title: Tokens minted on the destination equal tokens locked on the source
templates.statement: ghostMinted <= ghostLocked (no mint without a corresponding lock)
templates.harm: minting without locking is infinite-mint / bridge drain

templates.title: A message / signature / nonce cannot be consumed twice
binds: the consume path (relay/execute/permit) keyed by nonce or message hash
templates.statement: replaying an already-processed message/nonce MUST revert
templates.harm: replay = double-spend of a cross-chain mint or double-execution of a governance action

templates.title: A stale / zero / extreme oracle reading is rejected, never mispriced
templates.statement: an op priced off a stale/zero/extreme reading reverts or clamps — it never transacts at the bad price
templates.harm: mispricing off a bad oracle lets an attacker borrow/redeem at a wrong value (drain)

templates.title: Moving an on-chain readable within a block cannot be monetized
binds: the readable being moved (spot reserve, balance)
templates.statement: an atomic move-price -> act -> restore sequence does not net the actor a profit
ghosts: uint256 _actorEquityFloor  // snapshot before the manipulation sequence
templates.harm: spot-price / flash-loan manipulation extracts protocol value in one transaction

templates.title: Every minted token has exactly one owner and supply <= max
templates.statement: totalSupply <= MAX_SUPPLY and ownerOf(id) is a single non-zero address for minted id
templates.harm: minting past max or dual ownership breaks scarcity / lets a token be stolen

templates.title: Counted voting power equals the snapshot balance
templates.statement: Σ counted votes for a proposal <= snapshot supply (no double-count via transfer/delegate mid-vote)
templates.harm: double-counted votes let a whale pass a proposal they shouldn't (governance capture)

templates.title: A proposal cannot execute twice
binds: the execute path keyed by proposal id
templates.statement: executing an already-executed proposal MUST revert
templates.harm: re-execution replays a payout/parameter change (drain or takeover)

templates.title: Phase-gated actions revert outside their phase
templates.statement: an action legal only in phase X reverts in every other phase; terminal phases stay terminal
templates.harm: acting outside the intended phase (bid after close, claim before vest) breaks the sale

templates.title: The highest bid only increases; outbid funds stay refundable
templates.statement: highestBid never decreases; a previously-outbid actor can always withdraw their refund
templates.harm: a decreasing high bid or a locked refund lets an attacker win cheaply or trap funds

templates.title: The withdrawal queue conserves principal and cannot double-withdraw
templates.statement: ghostQueued == ghostCompleted + _pendingWithdrawals(); the same stake cannot be withdrawn twice
templates.harm: double-withdraw or lost queue entries drain staked principal

templates.title: A filled intent pays out exactly what was authorized
templates.statement: actualOut(intent) <= authorizedOut(intent); a solver cannot extract surplus beyond the stated fee
templates.harm: surplus extraction / over-payout on a filled intent steals user or protocol value

templates.title: A callback cannot observe or exploit a mid-update state
binds: the entry point that makes an external call before finishing its state update
templates.statement: re-entering any entry point from a token/receiver hook mid-call cannot break solvency/accounting
templates.tolerance: the paired solvency/conservation property is the oracle
templates.harm: classic reentrancy: drain via a state read/update ordered around an external call
templates.derived_via: library (proc 10 cross-contract composition; persona: reentrancy composer)
